votes.reason: JPM is the most direct large-bank way to hold my Financials call (a +45 bp steepening curve, a Fed on hold and Basel III capital relief), it is moving with XLF (+5.7% on the month, near its high), and its main risk this week, a sub-50K NFP turning into a credit scare, is one the whole call already carries.

Its +16% earnings week is part of the evidence my Healthcare thesis rests on, and as a biotech that barely tracks SPY it gives the book the cushion against Friday's jobs report that the call is there to provide; LLY's Aug 6 report is a risk for the whole sector, not a reason against this name.

UNH sits inside my Healthcare call as a defensive name that moves less than the market, and as a health insurer it is less exposed than the drug makers to LLY's Aug 6 report, the sector's biggest swing factor; its weak month (-2.6%) is not a sector reason against it, though with REGN it puts 45% of the book in Healthcare.

PEP is a big multinational staple that gets exactly the tailwinds my Staples call rests on (the dollar index below 100 lifting foreign earnings, oil down 5% easing packaging and freight costs), and its +2.1% week matches XLP keeping pace with SPY as the book's hedge for Friday.

SCHW fits my Financials call as a direct play on a steeper curve and a Fed on hold, since it earns more on client cash while short rates stay high, and it is the strongest financials trend on the sheet (+8.5% on the month, +18.8% over 12 weeks), with only the jobs-report risk the call already accepts.
